title: pvPrincipalComponentAnalysis
body:
## pvPrincipalComponentAnalysis Extends pvMulticorrelativeStatistics with the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix (optionally normalized, or robust using medians), and assesses data by projecting each observation onto the principal components, using the full basis, a fixed number of components or enough components to reach a fixed energy fraction. Use it to find dominant correlated modes among several fields or to reduce their dimensionality. Output port 0 is the statistical model (a multiblock of tables) and port 1 the input with assessment arrays added; select them with {"node": id, "port": n}. Common mistakes and assumptions: - Without normalization, variables with large variance dominate the components; choose Normalize using covariances when units differ. - Task 3 (Model and assess the same data) assesses data that also trained the model, which flatters the fit; prefer a separate data set via ModelInput. - Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation. Native constructor: `PrincipalComponentAnalysis`. Identity: `filters/PCAStatistics`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`. ### Inputs | Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: The input to the filter. Arrays from this dataset will be used for computing statistics and/or assessed by a statistical model. Accepted data: image data (uniform rectilinear grids) (vtkImageData); rectilinear grids (vtkRectilinearGrid); curvilinear structured grids (vtkStructuredGrid); polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData); unstructured grids (vtkUnstructuredGrid); tables (rows and columns) (vtkTable); graphs (vertices and edges) (vtkGraph). The input needs at least one point- or cell-centred array. | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkImageData","vtkRectilinearGrid","vtkStructuredGrid","vtkPolyData","vtkUnstructuredGrid","vtkTable","vtkGraph"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` | | `ModelInput` | Optional data input for the native ModelInput port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: A previously-calculated model with which to assess a separate dataset. This input is optional. Accepted data: tables (rows and columns) (vtkTable); multiblock datasets (vtkMultiBlockDataSet). | False | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkTable","vtkMultiBlockDataSet"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` | ### Options | Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `AttributeMode` | Attribute association whose arrays are analysed; VariablesofInterest names are looked up in it. Chosen by the ParaView entry text: "Point Data", "Cell Data", "Vertex Data", "Edge Data", "Row Data" or "Field Data". ParaView offers only the associations the connected input has (for example "Row Data" for a table), so a text it does not offer fails with NATIVE_DOMAIN_MISMATCH when the node is configured. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Point Data","Cell Data","Vertex Data","Edge Data","Row Data","Field Data"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Point Data"` | | `BasisEnergy` | The minimum energy to use when determining the dimensionality of the new space into which the assessment will project tuples. | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` | | `BasisScheme` | When reporting assessments, should the full eigenvector decomposition be used to project the original vector into the new space (Full basis), or should a fixed subset of the decomposition be used (Fixed-size basis), or should the projection be clipped to preserve at least some fixed "energy" (Fixed-energy basis)?

As an example, suppose the variables of interest were {A,B,C,D,E} and that the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix for these were {5,2,1.5,1,.5}. If the "Full basis" scheme is used, then all 5 components of the eigenvectors will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple in the original data into a new 5-components space.

If the "Fixed-size" scheme is used and the "Basis Size" property is set to 4, then only the first 4 eigenvector components will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple into the new space and that space will be of dimension 4, not 5.

If the "Fixed-energy basis" scheme is used and the "Basis Energy" property is set to 0.8, then only the first 3 eigenvector components will be used to project each {A,B,C,D,E}-tuple into the new space, which will be of dimension 3. The number 3 is chosen because 3 is the lowest N for which the sum of the first N eigenvalues divided by the sum of all eigenvalues is larger than the specified "Basis Energy" (i.e., (5+2+1.5)/10 = 0.85 > 0.8). | `{"type":"enum","values":["Full basis","Fixed-size basis","Fixed-energy basis"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Full basis"` | | `BasisSize` | The maximum number of eigenvector components to use when projecting into the new space. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` | | `NormalizationScheme` | Before the eigenvector decomposition of the covariance matrix takes place, you may normalize each (i,j) entry by sqrt( cov(i,i) * cov(j,j) ). This implies that the variance of each variable of interest should be of equal importance. | `{"type":"enum","values":["No normalization","Normalize using covariances"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"No normalization"` | | `RobustPCA` | Compute robust PCA with medians instead of means. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` | | `Task` | Specify the task to be performed: modeling and/or assessment.

  1. "Detailed model of input data," creates a set of output tables containing a calculated statistical model of the entire input dataset;
  2. "Model a subset of the data," creates an output table (or tables) summarizing a randomly-chosen subset of the input dataset;
  3. "Assess the data with a model," adds attributes to the first input dataset using a model provided on the second input port; and
  4. "Model and assess the same data," is really just operations 2 and 3 above applied to the same input dataset. The model is first trained using a fraction of the input data and then the entire dataset is assessed using that model.
When the task includes creating a model (i.e., tasks 2, and 4), you may adjust the fraction of the input dataset used for training. You should avoid using a large fraction of the input data for training as you will then not be able to detect overfitting. The Training fraction setting will be ignored for tasks 1 and 3. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Detailed model of input data","Model a subset of the data","Assess the data with a model","Model and assess the same data"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Detailed model of input data"` | | `TrainingFraction` | Specify the fraction of values from the input dataset to be used for model fitting. The exact set of values is chosen at random from the dataset. | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` | | `VariablesofInterest` | Choose arrays whose entries will be used to form observations for statistical analysis. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` | Execution contract: ```json { "mode": "serial", "performance": "unknown" } ``` Coverage and unbound native properties: ```json { "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options", "gaps": {}, "origin": "generated", "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available", "outputPorts": 2, "qualification": "not-run" } ``` ### Syntax example Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer. ```json { "id": "result", "filter": "pvPrincipalComponentAnalysis", "inputs": { "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input" } } ```
